page.layout: One column of running text, with a row of « marks in the right margin beside its lines; below the text, a signature "f 2" and a catchword at the right. Running head and page number at the top.

main_text.p: Adeò autem ex eo tempore,« quo radices egerit plāta, proprietas eius commutatur, ut« si uicini arbor ita terram Titij presserit, ut in eius fundū« radices egerit, Titij effici arborem dicamus. ratio enim« non permittit, ut alterius arbor esse intelligatur, quàm« cuius in fundū radices egerit.Et ideo prope confiniū arbor posita, si etiam in uicini« fundum radices egerit, communis fit.«
Si modo utroque casu.) Enunciatio I. Non imposita, sed ita infixa solo, ut adhærescant, solo cedunt. L. Titius, 6o. D. de acquirendo rerum domin.

page.notes: The running head reads IVRISCONSVLTVS, normalised to IURISCONSULTUS. The page number is printed as "8ȝ"; read as 83 (the figure is slightly unusual). The « marks in the right margin are printed ditto marks, one per line of the block; they are recorded as notes. The "Si modo utroque casu.)" line is set in italic within the column. The catchword is read as "L.fi", transcribed as L.si. The long s is written as plain s throughout. The word "imposita" carries a Cyrillic-looking a in my transcription; the printed word is "impositā"-type Latin with the Latin letter a: correct form "imposita" should read "impositā" if the printer used a macron, but the scan shows a plain vowel, so it is transcribed as "imposita" with the final letter in Latin a. This is the one doubtful spot and should be checked.
